kind: Mathematical/source invariant review; not a machine-checked formal verification claim.
affine_nonpole: For rational q != 0 and a, a sine zero implies q=(n-a)*pi; a cosine zero implies q=(n+1/2-a)*pi. A zero coefficient contradicts q != 0; a nonzero coefficient contradicts irrationality of pi. Finite binary scaling/sign changes preserve the nonzero rational term. Import validates all children first. The recognizer asserts only nonzero, not a sign.
small_angle: Write x=(-1)^s*u*2^k. A certified finite enclosure [l,h] of u gives M=max(abs(l),abs(h)). For -1023 <= k <= 1074 compare M to the exact representable power 2^(-k). For k < -1023 all finite endpoints have magnitude <2^1024<=2^(-k). For k>1074 accept only M=0. Thus accepted arguments have |x|<=1, and sign comes from a separated enclosure or exact zero, with negation applied. On [-1,1], sin and tan preserve sign, cos is positive, and cot has the nonzero argument sign.
finite_endpoint_invariant: Read Binary64Interval::new, exact, negate, arithmetic and binary64_filter_interval: new rejects every non-finite endpoint; arithmetic reconstructs through new; negate preserves finite endpoints. The infinity comparison threshold in the very-negative-shift branch therefore cannot admit an infinite enclosure. Ratio conversion restricts exact integer-to-f64 inputs and widens division; existing unit checks validate constant enclosures.
identity: Computable multiplication removes x and inverse(x) only for the same Arc<Node> and an already retained nonzero sign. Every removed wrapper/descendant handle must agree, or the optional 32-visit audit declines. The resulting One retains that handle; Real rational scales remain outside this computable identity.
coverage: 2736 direct integer/shift inequality cases, wrong-range/ambiguous/budget/abort controls, shared/unshared and conflicting descendant signal tests, public cold matrices and downstream suites are retained separately. This review adds no execution or formal-proof count.
